RagShortTexts: Situated across critical crossroads, Burgundians maintained fortified border networks anchored against rivers, mountain passes, and dense forests.
Under intense pressure from migrating populations and rival expansion, the borders faced acute strain from regional upheavals.
Frontier governors exercised broad emergency prerogatives, maintaining patrol outposts and garrison bastions to shield agrarian heartlands.

Variants.Content: The territorial perimeter of Burgundians spanned treacherous terrain encompassing river crossings, mountain defiles, and primeval woodlands. Shielding the arterial supply corridors leading toward Oder & Upper Main River, the regime garrisoned fortified outposts and watchtowers tasked with round-the-clock reconnaissance. In 374 AD, strategic volatility reached a fever pitch, aggravated by border clashes and cross-frontier raiding. Provincial commanders operated under persistent resource deficits, forced to contain covert banditry while preparing against full-scale royal invasions, knowing that any fatal rupture along the forward limes would unleash catastrophic devastation upon undefended inland communities.

Sentries on the Oder bridge count the rafts drifting downstream, and they report any boat that does not answer the password. Whenever a patrol returns, the captain marks the position of each raider sighting on the wax map. The guard at the palisade gate keeps a spear across his knees all night, watching the dark bank where the reeds grow thickest.

Raiders from the east have crossed the upper Main twice this summer, and the river villages are short of spears. Propose to neighboring counts a shared watch on the bridges for a fixed share of the toll. Keep the offer confidential until the other lords agree, since an open pact will draw the king's suspicion.
